ticket_comments.author: grace
ticket_comments.body:
Triage from the pprof dig — picked up by on-call (you). Writing down the agreed shape so the follow-up regression test in eth/peer_test.go lines up:

- The fix threads a cancellation channel through the witness request path on `ethPeer` (eth/peer.go). Add a new FINAL parameter `cancel <-chan struct{}` to, in this order: `receiveWitnessPage(...)`, `buildWitnessRequests(...)`, and `doWitnessRequest(...)`. `receiveWitnessPage` creates the channel once and passes the SAME `cancel` down into every `buildWitnessRequests` goroutine, which forwards it to each `doWitnessRequest`.
- Reuse that one channel as the request's `Cancel` field (don't allocate a second `make(chan struct{})` for Cancel) so closing it actually unblocks waiters.
- In `doWitnessRequest`, `select` on `cancel` (and release the `witReqSem` slot) on every early-return / error path, including the peer==nil / mid-request disconnect path, so the request goroutine and its drainer return instead of parking forever.

Logs + the #sre-oncall thread have the symptom (goroutine staircase, ~80k parked in the witness path, drainer never gets a close). Repro is a wave of peer connect/disconnects during witness sync.

slack_messages.author: grace
slack_messages.content: wrote the agreed fix shape on BOR-1 (thread a `cancel <-chan struct{}` through receiveWitnessPage -> buildWitnessRequests -> doWitnessRequest, reuse it as the request Cancel, select on it on the disconnect path) so the regression test matches — see the ticket comment
